To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a fructose-maltrodextrin carbohydrate-electrolytes solution with a ratio of 0.5 (4.5 and9%) was not different to water in terms of exogenous carbohydrate oxidation, gut comfort or performance.
the 0.5, 0.8, and 1:2.5 ratios of fructose to maltodextrin, ingested at 90 g/h, resulted in exogenous CHO oxidation rates of 1.0 ± 0.2, 1.1 ± 0.3, and 1 ± 0 g/min, respectively.
a 0.8:1.25 ratio of maltodextrin to fructose in a sports drink is more beneficial to endurance performance and gut comfort than a 1:1 ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the ratio of carbohydrates on exogenous carbohydrate oxidation, gut comfort, performance, and the relationship between exogenous carbohydrate oxidation and performance.
the effects of carbohydrate ingestion on performance and gastrointestinal discomfort in endurance athletes.
the effect of carbohydrate-electrolytic solution composition on the performance of athletes during exercise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
0.8 and 1.0 ratios of fructose to maltodextrin are the best ratios of carbohydrate to use during exercise.

the 0.5, 0.8, and 1-25 ratios of carbohydrate ingestion during exercise have a similar effect on exogenous carbohydrate oxidation but the ingestion of 0-8 and 1-2-5 ratios have a similar effect to the 0-5 ratio on performance.
0.8 and 1.2 ratios are better than 0.5 ratio, but the difference between the two ratios is not significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
0.8:1 fructose-maltose ratio in carbohydrate-salt solutions is a good choice for endurance performance.
the 0.5:1.0 ratio (by weight) for fructose: maltodextrin was the least effective of the three solutions tested.
the ratio of fructose to maltodextrin is important for the rate of exogenous carbohydrate oxidation and for gut comfort, but the magnitude of effect is small.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are likely small improvements to exogenous carbohydrate oxidation and endurance performance from ingesting a carbohydrate-electro-lyte solution with a fructose-maltose ratio of 0.80 to 1.00.
a fructose-maltose mixture with 0.5 to 0.8 ratio of fructose to maltose is the most optimal.
a 0.8 fructose to maltodextrin ratio may be the best option to maximize oxidation and performance and minimize gastrointestinal discomfort.
